outcome_detail: Filed July 9, 2026, in New York State Supreme Court, Bronx County; no resolution reported as of July 2026.
criminal_detail: No criminal charges against Deputy Inspector Juan O. Moran had been reported as of July 2026. (The separate criminal case against Inspector Jeremy Scheublin, arising from a different lawsuit at the same precinct, is covered in companion record rec-60.)
incident_date_approx: Alleged conduct during the plaintiffs' service at the 46th Precinct in the Bronx, reported in coverage from 2026.
description: An NYPD sergeant and two police officers filed a lawsuit on July 9, 2026, in New York State Supreme Court, Bronx County, against the City of New York, Police Commissioner Jessica S. Tisch, and Deputy Inspector Juan O. Moran. The complaint alleges sexual harassment, hostile work environment, retaliation, and race, ethnicity and national-origin discrimination under the New York State and New York City Human Rights Laws, arising from the plaintiffs' time at the 46th Precinct. According to the complaint, Moran sexually harassed the three women in various ways, including giving an unwanted tight hug, making sexual comments, and untying a knot securing one officer's dress. The plaintiffs said in a joint statement that the department knew of serious sexual-misconduct concerns tied to the precinct before their allegations and failed to protect them. The case is ongoing.
notes: Companion record to rec-60 (N.T. v. NYPD/Scheublin): a second, separate suit from the same 46th Precinct scandal, filed against a different supervisor. Plaintiffs (Sgt. Osmairys A. Avila and Officers Pamela Sosa and Brittany N. Romero) are named publicly as plaintiffs, not as accused officers.
